full_judgment:
Amirul Kabir Chowdhury J: Government of Bangladesh represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Fisheries and livestock and 4 other writ respondents seek leave to appeal against the judgment and order dated 10.05.2005 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in writ Petition No. 1186 of 2004 (heard analogously with Writ petition No.6591 of 2004) making the rules absolute. 

 2. Civil Petition for leave to Appeal No. 989 of 2005 has been Preferred against the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 1186 of 2004, in making the rule absolute. 

 3. Civil petition for leave to Appeal No. 990 of 2005 arises out of the aforesaid judgment and order passed by the High Court Division in making the rule absolute in Writ petition No. 6591 of 2004. 

 4. Civil Petition for leave to Appeal No. 58 of 2005 at the instance of Government of Bangladesh and six others arises out of order of the High Court Division in disposing of Writ Petition No.6073 of 2005 directing the writ respondent-petitioners to pay the arrear salaries and other benefits of the writ petitioner-respondents in the national pay scale with effect from 17 March 2003. 

 5. Civil Petitioner for leave to Appeal Nos. 989 and 990 of 2005 arising out of the same order passed by the High Court Division and Civil Petition for leave to Appeal No. 58 of 2005 also arising out of similar matters the three petitions are disposed of by this single order. 

 6. The writ petitioner-respondents moved the High Court Division in writ petition No. 1186 of 2004 challenging order dated 22.11.2003 (annexure-G to the writ petition) and for a direction to include the writ petitioners in the revenue budget with continuity of service and other attended benefits. 

 7. The writ petitioner-respondents of writ Petition No.6591 of 2004 moved the High Court Division challenging the legality of order dated 14.05.2003 (annexure-J to the writ petition) and for a direction to absorb them in revenue set up with continuity of service and other attended benefits. 

 8. In writ petition No.6073 of 2005 leading rise to Civil petition for leave to appeal No. 58 of 2005 the writ petitioners filed an application for direction upon the writ respondents to pay arrear salaries and other benefits to them and in all the writ petitions the High Court Division granted interim orders giving the directions as prayed for. 

 11. The respondents in Civil petition for leave to appeal No. 989 of 2005 in their application under article 102 of the Constitution stated that they were in the service of the Government in the 1st and 2nd livestock development projects since 1977 and were guided by recruitment rules approved by Chief Martial law Administrator through memo dated 16.10.1986 which is materially identical with the provision of Non-Gazetted Employees (Dept. to livestock Service) Recruitment Rules, 1985 and that in the project proforma of the project in question it was clearly shown that out of 1552 recruited employees, 1487 officers and staffs would be transferred to the revenue budget on completion of the project and that the Establishment Division sent recommendation of absorbing 854 posts including its incumbents with a condition that 170 employees would be directly transferred to the revenue budget and remaining 684 personnel would be transferred to the revenue budget by surrendering same number of vacant post from the revenue budget of Ministry of fisheries and in the meantime some of them already have been transferred to different revenue posts by the ministry of fishery and now 815 officers and staff are serving in the revenue set up while the petitioners have been waiting for regularization in revenue budget and that the ministry of finance issued circular for transferring 544 out of 815 posts in the revenue budget on certain per-conditions and being aggrieved by the said circular the writ petitioners preferred the above writ petitions and obtained rule. 

 12. In Civil petition for leave to appeal No.990 of 2005 the respondents stated in the writ petition that they were appointed by the Department of Bureau of Manpower, Employment Training, in short, BMET in 1st phase of a development project in the year 1988 and then transferred to 2nd phase of the same project in 1995 and that the project proforma of the project assured the employees of the project that on completion of the project the officers and staff of the project would be automatically transferred to revenue budget and will be regularized and the ministry of establishment made recommendation to transfer the officers and staff to revenue budget and agreed to absorb the petitioners on condition of surrendering 187 vacant posts of the BMET and the review committee of the ministry of finance recommended the petitioners to be absorbed in the revenue set up and that while the petitioners were waiting for regularization in the revenue set up, the secretary committee expressed their inability to absorb the petitioners in the revenue budget through memo dated 03.04.2003 in pursuance of which the petitioners services have been terminated by the BMET with effect from 03.04.2003 and hence they felt constrained to file the writ petition. 

 13. Both the writ petitions were contested by the Government stating, inter-alia, that although the ministry of Finance decided to transfer the post to revenue budget surrendering same number of vacant post and although such post was abolished by the ministry of manpower yet the sachib committee in the meeting held on 17.03.2003 did not find any reason to transfer those posts to the revenue budget and accordingly refused to accept the proposal of the Administrative ministry to absorb the writ petitioners in the revenue budget and that the Sachib committee is entitled to formulate any policy for the requirement of manpower and the leave petitions having no substance the rules are required to be discharged. 

 14. Civil petition for leave to appeal No. 58 of 2005 the writ petitioners alleged that they entered into the Service of the republic in a development project in 1988 and 1995 under the department of the Bureau of manpower, employment and training and in the project proforma it was provided that after completion in the project they would be transferred to revenue budget and that to facilitate absorption of the petitioners, the Administrative ministry of the petitioners, ministry of planning, Ministry of Establishment and standing Committee on Finance Ministry gave their full consent to absorb the services of the petitioners in the revenue set up and that while all steps were taken and hurdles were overcome to finally transfer them in the revenue set up Sachib committee headed by the Cabinet Secretary expressed inability to transfer the services of 187 posts to revenue set up without assigning any reason and as such they felt constrained to institute the writ petition. 

 15. In the aforesaid writ Petition No.6073 of 2005 the writ petitioners filed an application before the High Court Division praying for direction upon the respondents to pay their arrear salaries and other benefits. The High Court Division by order dated 21.08.2005 allowed the prayer directing the writ respondents i. e. the petitioners herein to pay their salaries as prayed for. 

 17. Mr. Abdur Rob Chowdhury, learned Counsel represented the respondent Nos.1-8 in Civil petition for leave to appeal Nos. 989 of 2005 and 990 of 2005 and respondent Nos.3, 4, 8, 9, 14, 20 and 21 in Civil petition for leave to appeal No.58 of 2005 and submits that the writ petitioners are legally entitled to be absorbed in the revenue set up as in the project proforma it was provided that after completion of the project they would automatically be absorbed in the revenue set up and mores the Ministries of establishment and finance duly recommended their absorption in the revenue budget and as such the High Court Division made the rule absolutes in writ petition Nos.1186 of 2004 and 6591 of 2004. 

 18. He further submits that considering the facts and circumstances and the judgment passed by the High Court Division in the aforesaid two writ petitions, the learned Judges of the High Court Division passed the impugned order on 21.08.2005 in Writ Petition No.6073 of 2005 giving the directions as prayed for and the aforesaid judgments and orders of the High Court Division do not call for any interference. 

 19. Mr. A. J. Mohammad Ali, learned Attorney General on the other hand submits that the learned Judges of the High Court Division erred in law in failing to consider the fact that as the writ petitioners appointment was time bound under the appointment letter, any alleged internal consideration about the regularization cannot make any legitimate expectation in the mind of the petitioners that their regularization in the revenue budget is guaranteed, and unless by any instrument of correspondence the government manifest its promise, on supposed violation of the same can be imposed upon the government. 

 20. He further submits that the regard being had to the fact that as the Government has no lack of authority in imposing pre-condition for the purpose of regularization in the revenue budget and so far as the creation of post in the revenue budget the Government has the discretion either to create of not to create post, which Government exercises on the basis of requirement and the court has no jurisdiction to compel the Government to create post in the revenue budget by applying the legitimate expectation of the writ petitioners and the principle of promissory estopple. 

 21. He thereafter submits that sometimes infrastructures along with manpower of Development project are transferred to revenue budget after completion of the project. This is done purely on the necessity of potentiality and fund availability of the Government and in this case the project was taken afresh in the 2nd phase. 

 25. The petitioners are permitted to prepare paper book out of court in accordance with rules.
